title: Polynomial algebras over Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay rings are Cohen–Macaulay
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] such that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$, its local ring $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] satisfies $\operatorname{depth}(R_{\mathfrak p})=\dim R_{\mathfrak p}$, where depth is as in [def-weil-pbc-depth] and Krull dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. For every integer $n\ge0$, the polynomial ring $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] is Noetherian and for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset P$ one has $\operatorname{depth}(P_{\mathfrak q})=\dim P_{\mathfrak q}$. Thus every finite-variable polynomial algebra over $R$ is Cohen–Macaulay, with that term meaning the displayed equality at all prime localizations.

source.place: Tag 00ND, lemma-CM-polynomial-algebra; proof: the ring case of lemma-maximal-CM-polynomial-algebra (Tag 0AAI).

proof.text: Induct on n. For n=0 the coefficientwise identification R[x_1,...,x_0]=R identifies the conclusion with the hypotheses, including Noetherianity. For the induction step assume the full assertion for n variables, set A=R[x_1,...,x_n], and identify the (n+1)-variable ring with B=A[X] by grouping monomials according to the exponent of the last variable.

source.place: Tag 00ND, lemma-CM-polynomial-algebra, and Tag 0AAI, induction on variables

proof.text: The induction hypothesis makes A Noetherian and gives depth(A_p)=dim(A_p) for every prime p of A. The A-algebra B=A[X] is generated by X, with presentation A[X]/(0), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes B Noetherian. This uses the existing finite-type permanence theorem for an arbitrary Noetherian coefficient ring, rather than the Z-only polynomial-Noetherian node.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence, applied in the induction of Tag 0AAI

proof.text: The coefficient description [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] writes B as the free A-module with basis 1,X,X^2,...: each polynomial has a unique finite expansion in these monomials. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], whose statement explicitly includes every free module, shows that A→B is flat.

source.place: Tag 0AAI, flatness of the polynomial extension; free-module flatness as in Tag 051G

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary prime q of B and let p=q∩A. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps], Step 3 gives a flat local homomorphism A_p→B_q, and both local rings are Noetherian by Step 2. Define F=B_q/pB_q. The closed-fibre clause of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-depth-formula] says that F is a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal qB_q/pB_q; its depth equality also applies to this map.

source.place: Tag 00HT, lemma-flat-localization (6), Tag 00FN, and Tag 0337, lemma-apply-grothendieck

proof.text: Put D=A/p, W=A\p, and k=κ(p)=Frac(D). Coefficient reduction gives B/pB=D[X], not k[X]. Every w∈W is outside q and hence is a unit in B_q. Inverting these constants after coefficient reduction gives W^{-1}(D[X])=k[X]. Write Q=W^{-1}(q/pB), the extended prime of k[X]. It is proper: a constant from W cannot lie in q. Under coefficient reduction and localization, f/w belongs to Q exactly when f∈q, since q is prime and w∉q. Consequently F≅k[X]_Q. Explicitly, the map sends the class of f/g (g∉q) to f̄/ḡ. Conversely the coefficient fractions a/w map to the classes of a/w in F, and every polynomial outside Q is a unit there after clearing its constant denominator w∈W. These maps agree on coefficients and X and are inverse on fractions. Thus Q is the fibre prime after inverting A\p; it is not being identified with q/pB in D[X].

source.place: Tag 0AAI, fibre after contraction and localization; explicit fraction calculation using the definitions of polynomial ring and prime localization

proof.text: By [lem-pur-polynomial-field-pid], k[X] is a domain and all its ideals are principal. Split into Q=0 and Q≠0. If Q=0, k[X]_Q inverts every nonzero polynomial and is the field k(X). If Q≠0, write Q=(h) with h≠0. To see Q is maximal, let J=(g) contain Q. Write h=gu. Primality gives g∈(h) or u∈(h). In the first case J=Q. In the second case u=hv, whence h=ghv and cancellation in the domain yields 1=gv, so J=k[X]. Thus Q is maximal, and F=k[X]_(h) is a nonzero local domain with maximal ideal generated by the nonzero nonunit h/1. This argument allows every prime q of B.

source.place: Tag 030A, lemma-polynomial-domain-normal, field case of the proof (k[X] is a PID); elementary ideal argument for the two fibre-prime cases

proof.text: If Q=0, the field F=k(X) has just the prime ideal (0), so dim(F)=0 by [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Its maximal ideal is zero, and multiplication by its only element 0 is not injective on F≠0. Thus no nonempty regular sequence lies in this ideal, while the empty sequence is regular. By [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] and [def-weil-pbc-depth], depth(F)=0=dim(F).

source.place: Tags 00LI and 00LF, definitions of depth and regular sequences; field case of the fibre calculation

proof.text: If Q≠0, it is maximal by Step 6, so [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-maximal-localization-dimension] applied with one variable gives dim(F)=1. In the domain F, multiplication by h/1 is injective, and F/(h/1)≠0 since h/1 lies in its proper maximal ideal. Therefore the singleton (h/1) is a regular sequence in the maximal ideal by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and [def-weil-pbc-depth] gives depth(F)≥1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension] with the nonzero finite F-module F over the Noetherian local ring F from Step 4: its support is all Spec(F), since every prime localization of a nonzero ring is nonzero. Hence depth(F)≤dim(F)=1. Together with Step 7, the two cases give depth(F)=dim(F)=δ for δ=0 or 1.

source.place: Tag 00OP, lemma-dim-affine-space (one variable), Tag 00LK, lemma-bound-depth, and Tags 00LI/00LF

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-depth-formula] for the Noetherian flat local map A_p→B_q, depth(B_q)=depth(A_p)+depth(F)=dim(A_p)+δ, using the induction hypothesis and Steps 7–8. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] for the flat map A→B of Noetherian rings at q over p, dim(B_q)=dim(A_p)+dim(F)=dim(A_p)+δ. Comparing these two equalities gives depth(B_q)=dim(B_q), with δ=0 in the zero-fibre-prime case and δ=1 in the nonzero-fibre-prime case.

source.place: Tag 0337, lemma-apply-grothendieck, and Tag 00ON, lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total, applied in the polynomial induction of 00ND

proof.text: Since q was arbitrary, B=A[X] has the required depth equality at every prime, and Step 2 supplies Noetherianity. This proves the induction step and hence the assertion for all finite n. If R is the zero ring, each polynomial ring is zero and has no primes, so the local assertion is vacuous; the argument for a fixed q is needed only when such a prime exists.

proof_origin.place: Tag 00ND and the polynomial induction/localization route of Tag 0AAI, with the arbitrary-prime fibre calculation and its zero/nonzero cases written explicitly; the final depth/dimension comparison uses Tags 0337 and 00ON rather than the module-support calculation in 0AAI.
